header.title: Backend Engineer
header.subtitle: Pursuing clarity in an intricate world

about.summary:
I am Shin Wonseok, a fourth-year Backend Engineer who tries to understand the essence of a problem and the whole flow before jumping into implementation.

I started backend development with Java/Spring services, building an AI image generation service that handled 1M+ monthly requests and a Flyway-based migration and test automation setup tailored to Tibero DBMS. At Cupix, I design and improve backend architecture that connects construction-site video data with BIM files containing building design information to track progress, and improved the system so 20M+ field data records and 100M+ snapshots and events are reflected consistently across 6+ regions.

Working through problems where multiple systems interact taught me that preventing the same issue from recurring matters more than fixing it quickly. In that process, I learned that the more complex the problem is, the more important it is to organize evidence calmly, keep discussions from becoming unproductive, and connect the work to solutions the team can act on right away. I want to work as a Backend Engineer who traces root causes to the end and turns them into improvements the team can execute.

experience.position: Backend Engineer / Application Part Lead · Backend (Dec 2025–Present, led 3-person part)
experience.description: Global spatial AI SaaS company that connects building 3D design models with on-site 360° capture data to track construction progress and asset status. Across a Rails monolith, NestJS/Lambda microservices and 30+ processing agents, I built large-file processing pipelines, worked on multi-region data consistency and developer infrastructure, and have led a 3-person Application Part since Dec 2025.

achievements.title: Built a Large-Scale BIM Processing Pipeline and Improved Its Performance
details: Built a new NestJS service that parses BIM 3D models with hundreds of thousands of parts and produces AI classification drafts, designing it across three repositories including the infrastructure (Elastic Beanstalk) and the Rails integration layer

Cut geometry download from 19m30s to 3m17s on an 840K-object model by replacing up to 347K per-chunk HTTPS requests with roughly 700 WebSocket batch messages, keeping the existing path as the recovery route so the change could not affect correctness, and verifying byte-level equality by hash

Turned an extraction that died at 8,058MB with OOM into one that completes within an 8GB heap by moving to streaming, and cut storage from 6.4GB to 3GB by restructuring property storage with key dictionaries and compression

Measured why Aurora rejects large INSERTs before execution and found the control variable is statement bytes rather than row count (15 rejections for INSERT vs 1 for DELETE in the same run, 0.5–1MB vs ~100B), then switched batching to a byte budget that halves on each rejection and retries

Traced a failure where extractions stayed locked for up to 14 days because the failure record itself was lost, confirmed four root causes from logs and database measurements, and added a sweeper that checks job liveness in the queue to reclaim zombie rows

achievements.title: Multi-Region Data Consistency and Event Pipeline
details: Investigated and recovered 124 data inconsistency incidents reported across US, Australia, Europe, Singapore, Japan and Middle East regions, identifying root causes such as a path where changing category and work area together never published the change event

Built a validation API that breaks down mismatches between 3D model elements and field records into duplicates, missing rows, phase mismatches and negative diffs, and pinned a real customer case as a test to prevent regressions

Batched Kinesis event publishing by exact byte size at 90% of the shard limit (1MB, 1,000 records/sec) and retried only failed records on partial failure; the consuming Lambda stops at the first failure to preserve in-shard ordering
Replaced bulk updates with a single bulkWrite call and pinned the one-call behavior with a test

achievements.title: Developer Infrastructure and Application Part Leadership
details: Cut the CI test pipeline from 49m20s to 11m47s (76%). Profiling identified the bottleneck as the test data creation cascade (a single fixture call triggered 29 database operations); after documenting why three alternatives were rejected, I applied lightweight fixtures to 57 of 71 files
Added a CI gate that fails when a test exceeds its per-example time budget, plus a static analysis rule, so the suite cannot silently slow down again

Built an in-house PR review automation tool in Rust that the backend team uses instead of a commercial service. Measured the error patterns of AI review output across 218 real reports and 860 items, then implemented a validator that filters out citations to code that does not exist and findings with no evidence
Lead a 3-person Application Part: assign ownership areas, relay leadership and company-wide engineering meetings to the part, and present part results on a biweekly cadence

experience.description: Standardized the team's Tibero-based development and test environment while taking over follow-up development, test coverage and query performance for a delivery mutual aid insurance back office.

achievements.title: Completed a Delayed Insurance Back Office and Improved Its Tests and Queries
details: Joined a delivery mutual aid insurance back office late after it had been delayed by understaffing, built four contract-processing features (quotation, payment, contract approval, endorsement), and carried them through integration testing to QA deployment

Introduced characterization tests (unit and e2e) to inherited code that had zero test coverage by cataloging scenarios first, reaching roughly 70% coverage in the contract-processing area I owned and establishing a regression safety net

Reviewed the execution plan of every SQL statement my area issued using EXPLAIN PLAN and DBMS_XPLAN, and removed N+1 queries found by tracing repeated queries in list endpoints using fetch join and batch loading

Blocked lost updates that occurred when several staff endorsed the same contract concurrently by comparing contract versions (optimistic locking), verified with a concurrent-save test that exactly one commit succeeded and zero updates were lost

achievements.title: Improved Developer Productivity and Test Automation in a Closed DBMS Environment (Tibero)
details: Developed Tibero Docker/TestContainer, eliminating per-developer local test DB setup overhead and reducing team-wide environment configuration costs
Achieved 70% Docker image size reduction (1.5GB → 401MB) by applying zstd compression algorithm and removing unnecessary files
Integrated Tibero TestContainer into CI/CD pipelines, automating database-dependent tests and ensuring consistent test environments
Analyzed Flyway core logic and developed Tibero-specific dialect for automated DDL version control, streamlining schema deployment process
Released 3 internally validated projects as open source, contributing to the expansion of Tibero developer ecosystem

experience.description: Expanded MiriCanvas AI Drawing backend into production, from external AI model integrations to 1M+ monthly image generation requests and GPU/CDN cost optimization.

achievements.title: Built AI Image Generation Service Backend from Scratch
details: Scaled from early prototype to production system handling 1M+ monthly image generation requests reliably
Designed asynchronous processing pipeline integrating external AI model APIs (OpenAI, Stability AI)

achievements.title: Saved About $185 per Month per Instance through GPU Infrastructure Downsizing
details: Implemented request classification logic by characteristics (resolution, model) to optimize GPU resource utilization
Applied instance downsizing (g5.2xlarge → g5.xlarge) based on workload analysis
Reduced spot instance setup time by 40% (25min → 15min) through AMI optimization and prewarming strategy

achievements.title: Reduced CDN Costs 80%+ with Lambda@Edge Real-time Image Transformation
details: Implemented Lambda function for real-time PNG → WebP conversion at CloudFront origin response
Achieved 75% average file size reduction through image format conversion, reducing CDN transfer costs by 80%+
Designed architecture enabling gradual migration without modifying existing S3 storage

achievements.title: Stabilized Concurrency and Retries in AI Image Generation Pipeline
details: Reviewed paths where user retries or job reruns could process the same generation request twice
Organized job execution and result persistence around a generation request identifier so they run once
Improved generation state and result persistence so retries after external AI API failures do not drift
